notes:
Context: Pinecrest is a mid-market B2B SaaS that powers multi-channel customer support (chat, email, help center search). They've been on VendorX/OpenAI for 18 months and are evaluating Redwood to reduce inference cost and gain more predictable performance. Roadmap: start on Redwood Hosted for fast validation, then migrate to Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) if parity and SLA checks pass.

POC details: adapter layer built to maintain OpenAI-compatible request surface; uses redirect+shim so product code changes minimal. Tests executed: full prompt suite (150 cases), latency benchmark (p50/p95), reranker A/B on 10k historical conversations, end-to-end support agent latency under load (50->200 rps).

Findings:
- Cost: preliminary estimates show ~15-25% lower token cost on Hosted when batching & caching enabled; big wins expected on Dedicated with quantized variants.
- Latency: p95 for short responses ~140ms on Hosted in na-us-west, matches target; multi-turn sequences occasionally add ~30ms overhead due to KV cache warmups.
- Quality: 12/150 prompts had noticeable wording/regression (mostly in rare edge-case templates). Team flagged this as high-priority: "we can't accept any more than 3% drop in NPS for support agent responses".
- Function calling & streaming: function-calling mapping mostly works; small schema mismatch for one internal tool (order-status lookup). Streaming frames are slightly chunked differently; engineering asks if Redwood can provide an exact streaming chunk contract for SDK parity.

Legal & Security: Pinecrest requires EU data residency for EU customers and KMS integration for encryption-at-rest. Legal also wants retention-controls feature (ability to opt-out of logging).

Migration plan (high level):
1) Hosted POC (complete): validate APIs, run prompt/regression suite, confirm token accounting.
2) Dedicated pilot (3 months reserved capacity): benchmark sustained throughput, test failover/fallback to Hosted, SLA negotiation.
3) Rollout: phased routing by customer region, model variant canary, automated rollback on quality regression.

Commercials discussed: preliminary Dedicated pilot pricing proposed: 3-month reserved slot (~$40k commit) with usage overage tiers. They requested a straight comparison vs current VendorX spend and a modeled cost per ticket.

Open asks / action items for Redwood team:
- Provide explicit token counting examples for batching & streaming scenarios (dev note).
- Commit to assisting on prompt parity debugging (SE-run sessions to triage 12 failing prompts).
- Provide KMS/HSM integration guide and EU residency SLA language for redlines.
- Clarify streaming framing contract and function-calling schema parity; ideally a test harness.

Quote from CTO during POC wrap: "If we can match parity on the voice of the agent and show predictable economics, Dedicated makes sense — but regressions must be zero-tolerance for customer-facing flows."
